subject: Recap: Context-profile & cost targets — NovaCorp discovery
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Context-profile & cost targets — NovaCorp discovery

Alex — great chatting earlier. Quick post-call recap and my suggested next steps so we can get you a scoped pilot and a price anchor for budgeting. I pulled the ballpark numbers from the call and the sample CSV you sent; attached is the small CSV you dropped in the call (nova_context_stats_q2.csv).

Key notes from today's discovery:
- Primary use case: in-product assisted authoring + short summarization for customer support transcripts. Real-time UI where latency < 350ms P95 is desirable for prompt-complete flows.
- Current traffic profile (per your sample): ~120k requests/day; distribution is skewed — ~70% simple prompts (avg prompt tokens ~80, avg completion tokens ~60), ~25% mid-length (avg prompt 350 / completion 220), ~5% long context (avg prompt 4.5k / completion 600).
- Context needs: intermittent long-window sessions for case-history retrieval; roughly 8% of users require >8k context occasionally, and ~0.8% require 32k+ windows (rare, multi-document pulls). No sustained 128k usage expected today.
- Desired budget range you mentioned on call: $8k–$25k/month for inference spend (not counting engineering). You also mentioned internal target of ~$15–20 per 1M tokens as a benchmark for procurement.

Initial pricing & unit-econ perspective (very high level):
- Baseline model class (8k context optimized): assume 1.2M tokens/day -> ~36M tokens/month. At $18 per 1M tokens => $648/month. This is illustrative because completion vs prompt mix and long-window overheads materially change cost.
- Long-window overhead: requests that require >8k context often cause 3–6x per-request compute (KV cache inefficiencies + memory pressure). If 5% of requests are long-window and they average 4.5k prompt tokens, effective token accounting and GPU time can push unit costs up to $45–$75 per 1M tokens for that slice unless we use specialized routing (larger instance, batching, or quantized model).
- Practical blended target: to hit your stated budget band with the profile you shared, we should aim for a blended unit price in the $12–$22 per 1M tokens range depending on how much of the long-window traffic we can optimize via caching and prefixing.

Open items I need from you to firm an estimate: (if you can drop these in the Drive link or reply inline that'd be great)
1) A week's anonymized traffic sample with token counts per request (CSV ok) — this lets us simulate batching and cache-win rates.
2) SLA/latency hard limit: you mentioned ~350ms p95 — confirm whether 450ms is acceptable for long-window requests.
3) Expected growth horizon (3/6/12 mo) and any critical business dates for procurement.

Suggested next steps:
- We run a 2-week pilot: ingest sample traffic + run simulated workload to produce a model mix recommendation and an explicit $/1M blended price for a 3-month commit. Deliverable: pilot report + MOP (mutual action plan).
- If you want, I can put together two price anchors today: a conservative one (no long-window optimization) and an optimized one assuming 50% cache-win on repeated context.

I'll wait for the sample CSV (or confirmation that the attached is the right one). Marissa will help scope the pilot once we have the sample. Karthik will weigh in on which model/quantization profiles to recommend.

Thanks again — short action items: please share the 1-week sample + confirm latency for long-window flows.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

Vivek — thanks for the recap and thorough breakdown. A couple clarifications inline: 

- The attached CSV you included is correct; thanks for consolidating.
- The 120k req/day figure is the current production rate across our EU+US clusters; we expect 2x growth in 6 months if a pilot goes well.
- Latency: for standard prompts 350ms p95 is required. For long-window requests we can tolerate up to 700ms p95 (these are background or semi-async in the product).

Alex / Vivek — quick technical sketch from my side to make the pricing exercise reproducible. Adding this so procurement can see the levers.

Assumptions for pricing model (will adjust once we have the token-level week sample):
- Token accounting method: we charge on total tokens processed (prompt + completion) after any prefix caching and dedup.
- Cache-win: if a user repeats the same conversation head we can avoid re-sending the full prompt; simulated cache-win rates: 0% (no cache), 35% (moderate), 60% (aggressive) — we will simulate all three.
- Batching: for high-concurrency bursts we can batch smaller prompts to increase throughput; batching helps more for 8k sessions than 32k since memory footprint grows quickly.
- Model mix: propose two lanes for pilot: 1) 8k-optimized LLM (faster, cheaper per token) for ~95% of requests; 2) 32k-variant for long-window cases (provisioned with autoscale and a larger GPU family).

Concrete pricing anchors I will produce for the pilot (numbers are placeholders until we run sim):
- Conservative (no cache): blended $/1M tokens = $28
- Moderate (35% cache-win): blended $/1M tokens = $17
- Optimized (60% cache-win + quantization): blended $/1M tokens = $11

Notes on long-window multipliers:
- 8k requests typically ~1.8x compute per token vs short prompts due to KV maintenance at scale.
- 32k requests without prefix pruning can be 4x–6x; moving them to a separate 32k-optimized routing path reduces tail latency and cost by isolating resource pressure.

Deliverables for pilot (2 weeks):
1) Workload simulation report with token histograms + P95 latency estimates per lane.
2) Cost table: per-lane tokens, projected monthly spend, blended $/1M tokens under three cache scenarios.
3) Recommended model/instance mix and an ops playbook for long-window fallbacks (e.g., degrade to summary-only when concurrency > threshold).

Timing: once we have the sample, engineering can spin up the sim within 48–72 hours; report delivered end of pilot (week 2).

I'll start the baseline sim as soon as you drop the CSV. 

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
